title: Integrated Finance Policy: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document defines Redwood Inference’s integrated finance and legal operating policy for budgeting & forecasting, procurement and vendor contracting, procurement approvals, and revenue recognition & billing. It standardizes required controls, approval thresholds, accounting treatments (ASC 606-aligned), and operational steps to ensure consistent treatment across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private product lines.

Scope:
- Applies to all product and corporate spend, customer and partner contracts, procurement transactions, and revenue arrangements for Redwood Inference entities.
- Excludes acquisitions and equity transactions (handled by Corporate Development).

Goals:
- Ensure reliable forecasts and timely budget governance.
- Standardize procurement and contracting to reduce legal and compliance risk.
- Ensure consistent, auditable revenue recognition and billing procedures.

Key Definitions:
- Customer Contract: Any executed agreement that creates enforceable rights to consideration.
- Performance Obligation: A distinct good or service promised in a customer contract (ASC 606).
- Deferred Revenue: Contract consideration received (or invoiced) before performance is complete.
- One-time Setup Fee: Implementation or onboarding charge that may be distinct from ongoing subscription services.

Ownership and Roles:
- Finance (FP&A): Overall budgeting and forecast consolidation, monthly variance analysis, and reporting.
- Legal: Contract review, clause approvals, and escalation for non-standard terms.
- Procurement: Vendor selection, PO issuance, and supplier onboarding.
- Revenue Operations (RevOps): Billing schedules, invoice issuance, and collections.
- Product / Eng Owners: Provide technical and cost justification for budget requests and vendor selection.

Approval Matrix (summary):
- Expenses <= $5,000: Team Manager approval.
- $5,001 – $50,000: Department Head + Procurement review.
- $50,001 – $250,000: Finance Business Partner + Legal (if contract) + Procurement.
- > $250,000: Executive approval (CFO/CEO) + Legal + Procurement + Finance Director.
- Capital expenditures > $100,000: Must follow capital approval workflow and depreciation schedule.

Budgeting & Forecasting Process:
1. Annual Budget (Owned by FP&A)
   - Timeline: Planning kickoff in August; draft by October; executive review in November; board submission in December.
   - Components: Revenue by product line (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), COGS (GPU, cloud, infra ops), R&D, Sales & Marketing, G&A.
   - Assumptions: Document list-price, discount schedule, churn, paid conversion rates, average contract term.

2. Quarterly Forecasts
   - Rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly; formal reforecast each quarter.
   - Drivers: Sales funnel conversion, committed Dedicated contracts, expected capacity purchases.

3. Variance Reporting
   - Monthly close: FP&A publishes variance report within 7 business days after month end.
   - KPIs tracked: ARR (if applicable), MRR, monthly invoiced revenue, collections DSO, gross margin per product line.

Procurement Procedures (Vendor Selection to PO):
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist:
  - Completed vendor form in procurement system (including TIN/W-9 or equivalent).
  - Security questionnaire if vendor will access customer data or internal systems (InfoSec review required).
  - Insurance verification (minimum limits: general liability $1M, cyber $1M) where applicable.

- Competitive Selection:
  - For purchases > $50k, obtain at least 3 bids or documented justification for single-source.

- Purchase Order (PO) Requirements:
  - POs must reference approved budget code and be issued prior to start of work for purchases > $50k or where contract requires.
  - PO fields: vendor_name, vendor_id, scope_summary, budget_code, approver, amount, start_date, expected_delivery. (Procurement system captures these fields.)

- Approval Workflow:
  - Initiator submits requisition -> Manager approval -> Procurement review -> Finance validation -> Legal (if contract) -> Final approver as per matrix -> PO issuance.

Contracts & Legal Process:
- Standard Contract Types:
  - Master Services Agreement (MSA) for customers: default term 12 months, termination 30 days for convenience, 60 days for material breach.
  - Statement of Work (SOW): tied to MSA; must specify deliverables and acceptance criteria.
  - Data Processing Agreement (DPA): required for any processing of customer personal data.
  - NDA: standard mutual 3-year confidentiality period.

- Non-standard Terms Escalation:
  - Any requested change to liability cap, indemnity, data residency, or IP ownership requires Legal review and must be logged in the contract tracker with rationale and negotiation history.

- Contract Review Checklist (must be completed and attached to contract record):
  1. Counterparty legal name and authorized signee verified.
  2. Effective date and term clearly defined.
  3. Pricing, billing cadence, and payment terms documented.
  4. SLA and credits clearly described (if applicable).
  5. Security and data protections in place (DPA).
  6. Export controls / compliance clauses present where relevant.
  7. Approval evidence for any non-standard terms.

Contract Storage and CLM:
- All executed agreements must be uploaded to the Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system within 3 business days of signature and tagged with contract_type, owner, renewal_date, and revenue GL mapping.

Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy (Principles):
- Policy intent: Recognize revenue in accordance with ASC 606: identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize as obligations are satisfied.

- Product Line Examples and Treatment:
  1. Hosted API (Usage-based)
     - Transaction price: usage measured in tokens/embedding units; recognized as services are delivered (i.e., when API calls are made).
     - Invoicing: Monthly in arrears for usage during the prior month unless customer has prepay arrangement.
     - Deferred revenue: Not applicable for pure pay-as-you-go usage (no billing in advance).

  2. Dedicated (Reserved Capacity)
     - Transaction price: committed monthly or annual fees for reserved GPUs.
     - Recognition: Ratably over the commitment period (recognized on a straight-line basis over the term).
     - Upfront prepayments: recorded as deferred revenue and amortized over the committed term.

  3. Private (License / On-prem + Support)
     - Distinct deliverables (license, implementation, support): allocate transaction price to each performance obligation.
     - Setup fees: assess whether distinct; if not distinct from ongoing services, recognize over the expected service period (typical amortization 12 months).

- Contract Modifications:
  - Treat changes as either a separate contract (if additional distinct goods/services at standalone price) or a modification to the existing contract (prospective or cumulative catch-up) per ASC 606. Legal + RevOps must document and route modifications through CLM.

- Variable Consideration and Refunds:
  - Variable fees (usage credits, rebates, SLA credits) are estimated and constrained if they are subject to significant reversal. Document the estimation method and update monthly.
  - Refunds/credits: post an adjusting entry when credit is agreed; if invoiced, reduce accounts receivable and revenue as appropriate.

Billing & Collections:
- Standard Terms: Net 30 from invoice date unless negotiated otherwise.
- Invoice cadence: Monthly in arrears for usage; monthly/quarterly for committed capacity; annual prepay accepted for Dedicated with discounts.
- Invoice fields: invoice_id (format: RWI-YYYYMM-#####), invoice_date, due_date, customer_name, contract_id, period_start, period_end, line_items (description, qty, unit_price, amount), tax_summary, total_due, payment_instructions.
- Payment Methods: ACH / Wire / Credit Card for self-serve customers via payment gateway. Large enterprise customers support invoicing with PO numbers.
- Collections: Past-due >30 days -> automated reminders; >60 days -> Sales handoff + collections hold; >90 days -> Legal escalation and potential service suspension per contract.

Accounting and GL Mapping (sample codes):
- Revenue Hosted API: GL 4000
- Revenue Dedicated: GL 4010
- Revenue Private (license/support): GL 4020
- Deferred Revenue: GL 2300
- Rebates and Credits: GL 5400
- COGS - Cloud/GPU: GL 5000

Monthly Close Checklist (Finance Owner: Accounting Manager):
1. Reconcile invoice register to AR subledger.
2. Reconcile deferred revenue beginning and ending balances; post monthly amortization journal for committed contracts.
3. Review revenue estimates for variable consideration; document changes.
4. Verify CLM mapping of new contracts and ensure GL mapping is present.
5. Produce revenue roll-forward and share with FP&A and RevOps.

Controls and Audit Evidence:
- Evidence required for each recognized revenue item: executed contract or SOW, pricing schedule, usage reports (for usage-based revenue), evidence of performance (API logs or provisioning records), and invoice.
- Internal audit cadence: annual SOC/financial audit; quarterly control self-assessments for revenue and procurement cycles.

Exceptions and Escalations:
- Exceptions to approval thresholds must be documented with business justification and signed off by Finance Director and Legal Counsel.
- Escalation path: Requestor -> Manager -> Finance Business Partner -> Legal (if contract) -> Finance Director -> CFO.

Operational Templates and Examples (appendix):
- Sample Invoice Line (text):
  "2026-01 Usage: Hosted API text-generation (10,000,000 tokens) — 10,000,000 tokens @ $0.0005/token = $5,000.00"
- Sample PO description: "Dedicated - 8x A100 reserved GPU capacity (12-month) - monthly fee $40,000"
- Sample Contract Clause IDs to track in CLM:
  - CL-TERM (term and termination)
  - CL-LIMIT (liability cap)
  - CL-DPA (data processing)
  - CL-SLA (service levels and credits)
  - CL-EXPORT (export controls)

Appendix A — Quick Reference Approval Thresholds:
- Team purchases <= $5k: Manager
- Department purchases $5k-$50k: Department Head + Procurement
- Major purchases > $250k: Executive (CFO/CEO) + Legal + Procurement

Appendix B — Contact List:
- Finance (FP&A): fpna@redwoodinference.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwoodinference.com
- Legal: contracts@redwoodinference.com
- RevOps / Billing: billing@redwoodinference.com

Questions or requests for exceptions should be routed to procurement@redwoodinference.com.
